+## Guarded path identity repair
+
+The subsequent independent review identified that discovery received the original
+relative build argument even though validation returned an absolute identity.
+The callback's working directory could therefore select a different tree.
+`select_tests`, `selected_ctest` and the CLI now retain `Path(guard['build_dir'])`
+immediately after the static gate. Discovery, selection, metadata rechecks and
+the generated execution argv use that checked identity. The original argument
+is validated before conversion; symlink/aliased-tree rejection is unchanged.
+No second resolution of the caller's relative path determines the execution tree.
+
+Eight new inert regressions cover relative and absolute helper arguments with a
+different callback cwd, cwd changes after discovery/validation, both CLI branches,
+direct selection, unsafe relative trees and relative symlink rejection. The
+pre-fix reproduction (four failures/one error among eight methods) is retained;
+after repair all eight and the existing39 inert methods pass (47 total). These
+tests fake all discovery/execution and block real process launch; no CTest or
+GPU command runs. The exact19 CPU plan and supported flat layouts are unchanged.
+
+Evidence: `results/raw/ctest_path_repair_20261010T234224414430Z/FINAL_AUDIT.md`.
+Only the two changed source identities were explicitly renewed in the local
+selection manifest; classifications, commands and metadata policy were preserved.
+Separate independent review remains required before prerequisites or study launch.
+The quiescent-tree and trusted-tool limitations above still apply.
